$comment: Rectangles are in logical 270x480 engine pixels (9:16, matches the 1080x1920 output at *4). Every important text element (subtitles, on_screen_text, source_plate, AI plates) must stay inside the intersection of all enabled platforms' safe zones for a given release, so templates use the tightest common rectangle unless they target one platform only.
sourcing_note: Per-platform rectangles below are conservative engineering estimates, not numbers copied from a live, currently-fetched official guide: YouTube's, TikTok's and Instagram's own safe-zone pages (support.google.com, ads.tiktok.com/business/creativecenter, facebook.com/business/help) were unreachable from this sandbox at the time this file was written (403/404/blocked, consistent with other platform domains being blocked here -- see notes). The margins follow the well-known general shape repeatedly published by third-party creator tools (reserve roughly the top ~5-8% for a status/caption bar, the bottom ~15-20% for username/caption/music ticker, and the right ~20-25% for the like/comment/share icon column on TikTok and Instagram specifically), erring conservative. Re-verify against each platform's current official safe-zone guide with a working fetch before this ships to production, and update this file plus `common_safe_rect` if the real numbers differ.

youtube.source: Engineering estimate, not independently verified in this sandbox (see sourcing_note). YouTube Shorts' own on-screen UI (title, channel handle, like/comment/share column) is generally considered the lightest of the three platforms.

tiktok.source: Engineering estimate, not independently verified in this sandbox (see sourcing_note). TikTok reserves the widest right-hand icon column and a deep bottom caption/sound band of the three platforms.

instagram.source: Engineering estimate, not independently verified in this sandbox (see sourcing_note). Reels reserves a shorter top strip than TikTok but a deep bottom caption band and a right-hand action column.

common_safe_rect_note: Intersection of the three platform rectangles above, in logical pixels; nes-desk and night-report both key their plate/subtitle placement to this rectangle so one render clears all three platforms.
